scope.evidence: Every edit serves the ticket: two models, the IssueTicket/UpdateQueue actions, both factories, two migrations, four test files, and the required docs (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md). The docs/api/totem.md example is updated only to the new code format, and no UI, totem endpoint, call-ordering or unrelated refactor was added.

issues.explanation: down() re-adds unique(queue_id, code) after dropping issue_date; once the new daily sequence has legitimately produced the same code on two issue dates, rollback will fail with a duplicate-key error, so the migration is not practically reversible.

The requirement to backfill existing rows from DATE(issued_at) is implemented but never exercised; TicketSchemaTest only asserts the final column/index shape, so a regression in the backfill or the NOT NULL step would go unnoticed.
Using whereDate() wraps the DATE column in a SQL function; where('issue_date', $issueDate) is equivalent for a DATE column and keeps the predicate index-friendly.

The (string) $priority key lookup is unreachable after normalization (PHP/JSON arrays use integer keys) and the !== $priority/$level halves of the uniqueness guards can never be true for a single letter, so these branches add code without changing behavior.
The is_string() and default arms of the issueDate() mutator both do Carbon::parse($value)->toDateString(); they can be collapsed (and Carbon already satisfies DateTimeInterface).

The InvalidArgumentException catch around $queue->save() duplicates the ValidationException mapping already performed at lines 30-38, since the map is normalized before save; it adds noise without covering a realistic new failure.

review.summary: Implements daily, priority-prefixed ticket codes end to end: per-queue prefix maps with model-level validation, Ticket::nextCode scoped by queue/prefix/issue_date, single-clock issuance, factory alignment, two migrations, documentation and a broad Pest suite. Forward behavior meets every requirement and contract; the main caveats are a down() that cannot re-add the old unique index once cross-day duplicate codes exist and the untested DATE(issued_at) backfill, plus a handful of redundant checks.
